neighbours.label: Awkward, evasive behaviour in narration: shuffling feet, looking down or away, shifting, hesitation fillers like 'um' and 'uh', vs the same scenes told with confident or neutral action
fire: When the teacher asked who broke the vase, Tom just stared at his feet.
"So, um, do you want to get coffee sometime?" he asked quietly.
She shifted from one foot to the other, avoiding her father's gaze.
The boy mumbled an apology and looked down at his shoes.
"Uh, I think I left it somewhere," she said, glancing away.
Caught in the lie, he shuffled his feet and studied the carpet.
Marie twisted her fingers together, unable to look him in the eye.
He cleared his throat, eyes on the floor, and said nothing at all.
quiet: When the teacher asked who fixed the vase, Tom proudly raised his hand.
"So, do you want to get coffee sometime?" he asked with a grin.
She stepped forward and met her father's gaze with a smile.
The boy announced the news and looked up at the crowd.
"I left it on the kitchen table," she said, pointing over there.
Asked about the plan, he walked to the board and drew a map.
Marie folded the letter neatly and handed it to him.
He opened the window, looked at the sky, and started to sing.
